text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Renault poised to announce about 3,000 lay-offs in France as Belgian politicians threaten legal action to fight shutdown of the carmaker's Vilvoorde plant.
-- Court orders liquidation of Comipar and Pallas Stern banking subsidiary.
-- February unemployment up 0.6 percent over January.
-- Caisse des Depots sees 0.5 percent first-quarter GDP growth.
-- Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres says excluding Portugal from single currency would violate Maastricht treaty.
-- Alcatel Espace applies for FCC license to launch wide-band multimedia system of low-orbit satellites at a cost of $3.5 billion to compete with Globalstar and Iridium.
-- LVMH 1996 operating profit up six percent.
-- France Telecom restructures prices in run-up to 1998 deregulation.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene attacks Renault's move to shut down Belgian production unit as employees stage sit-in blocking 4,500 vehicles.
-- Libya to revamp foreign investment laws in a bid to attract more French capital.
-- Utilities supplier EDF posts 1.9 billion franc 1996 net profit.
-- Societe Generale Chairman Marc Vienot calls for piecemeal sell-off of Credit Lyonnais.
LE FIGARO
-- Economy minister of Belgium's Flemish region calls Renault plant shutdown an "act of terrorism".
-- President Jacques Chirac to press for 28 billion franc sale of 100 Airbus airliners during May trip to Beijing.
LIBERATION
-- Pallas Stern bankruptcy leaves eight billion franc loss.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Belgian officials call for boycott of Renault vehicles.
